data.title: Label
data.tagline: Visible text that tells people what a form control asks for
data.description: An Email label on a sign-in form should stay visible and focus its matching input when clicked. Put required, format, and error information nearby instead of relying on placeholder text.

distinctions.label: Tag
distinctions.explanation: Label explains what a control needs. Tag marks a content category, status, or filter.

distinctions.label: Form
distinctions.explanation: Label describes one control. Form organizes and submits a set of fields.

use: A clear name for complex controls
avoid: A placeholder used as the only label
A vague name such as Information or Content
A full help paragraph inside the label

lessonPractice.title: A registration form only uses Enter a value as placeholder text, so users cannot tell email from username after typing. What should change?

options.label: Keep a visible label for each field and make label clicks focus the associated input
options.feedback: A visible, associated label explains the field before and after entry and provides another way to focus it.

options.label: Change the placeholders to Email and Username but still hide them after entry
options.feedback: More specific placeholders still disappear, leaving users without field names when reviewing completed values.

options.label: Add mail and user icons and reveal each field description on hover
options.feedback: Icons can be ambiguous and hover explanations are unreliable on touch and keyboard, so they cannot replace labels.

data.agentPrompt: Add persistent visible labels for username, email, and password and associate each one with its input. Use placeholders only for examples, keep errors and format requirements nearby, and verify that clicking each label focuses the correct field.
